title: How far can ten fingers count?
hook: Ten fingers count to ten. Unless each finger means something different.

doesNotKnow: that n two-state places count 2^n different numbers

misconception: Ten fingers can show only ten numbers, or at most a hundred.
objective: The learner can explain that each up-or-down finger doubles the number of patterns, so ten fingers worth 1, 2, 4 ... 512 show every number from 0 to 1023: 1024 numbers.

claims.text: Ten fingers worth 1, 2, 4, ..., 512 add up to 1023 when all are up.
claims.source: 1 + 2 + ... + 512 = 2^10 - 1 = 1023; recomputed with node from the stage's VALUES.

claims.text: Ten fingers, each up or down, make 2^10 = 1024 different patterns.
claims.source: Each finger has 2 states independently: 2 x 2 x ... x 2 (ten times) = 1024.

claims.text: Every whole number from 0 to 1023 has exactly one finger pattern (its binary representation).
claims.source: Existence and uniqueness of binary representation, by induction on the number of places; 1024 patterns and 1024 numbers match one to one.

claims.text: Adding one more finger doubles the count: it can be down (all the old numbers) or up (each old number plus its value).
claims.source: Patterns with n + 1 places = 2 x patterns with n places.

recall.question: Using only 8 up-or-down switches worth 1, 2, 4 ... 128, how many different numbers (0 included) can you set?
recall.why: Each switch doubles the count: 2 multiplied by itself 8 times is 256, covering 0 to 255.
